components.note: 忄 (heart, 竖心旁) — marks feelings and mood, as in 怕 fear, 快 happy, 恨 hate; 忧 is worry and sadness.
尤 (yóu) — close sound: 忧 yōu vs yóu.
阝 (city, 右耳旁 on the right) — marks places, as in 都 capital, 邮 mail; the gloomy sense of 郁 is a borrowed one.
有 (yǒu) hints at the sound only loosely.

example.hanzi: 阴雨天总让她感到有点忧郁。
example.pinyin: yīnyǔtiān zǒng ràng tā gǎndào yǒudiǎn yōuyù.
example.english: Overcast, rainy days always make her feel a bit melancholy.
example.fact: Seasonal affective disorder, a form of depression tied to reduced sunlight in winter months, is thought to affect a meaningful share of people in temperate climates and is treated in part with bright light therapy — sitting in front of a specialized lightbox that mimics outdoor daylight intensity.

examples.hanzi: 他看起来有点忧郁，一句话也不说。
examples.pinyin: Tā kàn qǐlái yǒudiǎn yōuyù, yí jù huà yě bù shuō.
examples.english: He looks a bit melancholy and doesn't say a word.

examples.hanzi: 这首曲子带着淡淡的忧郁。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shǒu qǔzi dàizhe dàndàn de yōuyù.
examples.english: This piece of music carries a faint melancholy.

components.note: 扌 (hand radical, 提手旁) — actions by hand: 打, 拉, 推; 挑 is to pick out by hand.
兆 (zhào) is a loose sound clue; same part in 跳 tiào, 桃 táo and 逃 táo.
走 (walk, run) — movement, as in 赶 chase, 超 surpass, 越 cross over; 起 is to rise or get up.
己 (jǐ) is a loose sound clue for qǐ; 己 also sounds out 记 jì and 纪 jì.

example.hanzi: 那句话无意中挑起了两人之间的争吵。
example.pinyin: nà jù huà wúyì zhōng tiǎoqǐ le liǎng rén zhī jiān de zhēngchǎo.
example.english: That remark unintentionally stirred up an argument between the two of them.
example.fact: The assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand in Sarajevo in June 1914 is the textbook example of a single incident provoking a chain reaction — within about five weeks, a web of alliances pulled nearly all of Europe's major powers into what became World War I.

examples.hanzi: 这件事挑起了大家的好奇心。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn shì tiǎoqǐ le dàjiā de hàoqíxīn.
examples.english: This matter aroused everyone's curiosity.

examples.hanzi: 他故意挑起这场争论。
examples.pinyin: Tā gùyì tiǎoqǐ zhè chǎng zhēnglùn.
examples.english: He deliberately started this argument.

components.note: 广 (shelter) — buildings, as in 店 shop, 床 bed, 度 degree; 底 is the base of a house.
氐 (dī) is a close sound clue for dǐ; also in 低 dī and 抵 dǐ.
牛 (ox) — cattle and animals, as in 物 thing, 牧 herd, 牺 sacrifice: 特 first meant a bull, then special.
寺 (sì) is only a loose sound clue for tè; 寺 also in 诗 shī and 持 chí.
彳 (step) — walking and conduct, as in 行, 往, 得, 很.
聿 (brush) — writing the rules: 律 is law, and a rule of rhythm.

example.hanzi: 底特律曾经是美国汽车工业的中心。
example.pinyin: Dǐtèlǜ céngjīng shì Měiguó qìchē gōngyè de zhōngxīn.
example.english: Detroit was once the center of the American auto industry.
example.fact: Henry Ford's Highland Park plant in Detroit introduced the moving assembly line in 1913, cutting the time to build a Model T chassis from about 12 hours to roughly 90 minutes — a change so radical it reshaped not just car manufacturing but industrial production worldwide.

examples.hanzi: 底特律的冬天又冷又长。
examples.pinyin: Dǐtèlǜ de dōngtiān yòu lěng yòu cháng.
examples.english: Winters in Detroit are cold and long.

examples.hanzi: 他的哥哥在底特律的一家汽车厂工作。
examples.pinyin: Tā de gēge zài Dǐtèlǜ de yì jiā qìchēchǎng gōngzuò.
examples.english: His brother works at a car factory in Detroit.

components.note: 氵 (water) — water and liquids, as in 河, 海, 汤; water means life: 活 is alive.
舌 (shé, tongue) is a loose sound clue for huó; also in 话 huà.
土 (earth) — a green shoot pushing up from the ground: growth, birth, life. 生 also sounds out 性 xìng, 姓 xìng and 星 xīng.
土 (earth) — a green shoot pushing up from the ground: growth, birth, life. 生 also sounds out 性 xìng, 姓 xìng and 星 xīng.

example.hanzi: 这不是电影情节，是活生生的真实事件。
example.pinyin: zhè bú shì diànyǐng qíngjié, shì huóshēngshēng de zhēnshí shìjiàn.
example.english: This isn't a movie plot — it's a real, living event.
example.fact: Coelacanths, a lineage of fish once thought to have gone extinct 66 million years ago alongside the dinosaurs, turned out to be very much alive when a living specimen was caught off the coast of South Africa in 1938, stunning scientists and earning the fish the nickname 'living fossil.'

examples.hanzi: 画里的人物看起来活生生的。
examples.pinyin: Huà lǐ de rénwù kàn qǐlái huóshēngshēng de.
examples.english: The figures in the painting look lifelike.

examples.hanzi: 他活生生地把一块石头变成了艺术品。
examples.pinyin: Tā huóshēngshēng de bǎ yí kuài shítou biànchéng le yìshùpǐn.
examples.english: He turned a stone into a work of art as if it were alive.

components.note: 罒 (net, form of 网) — nets and entrapment: 罗 net, 罚 punish, 骂 scold; here a net of wrongdoing 非 catching the guilty.
非 (not, wrong) — what is wrong or unlawful; in 罪 it is the wrongdoing caught in the net.
木 (tree) — wood, as in 桌, 树, 板: 案 is a wooden table.
安 (ān) is a close sound clue for àn; also in 按 àn.

example.hanzi: 警方正在调查一起复杂的罪案。
example.pinyin: jǐngfāng zhèngzài diàochá yì qǐ fùzá de zuì'àn.
example.english: The police are investigating a complicated criminal case.
example.fact: Fingerprint identification became a standard tool in criminal cases only in the late 19th century, after Argentine police officer Juan Vucetich used a bloody fingerprint left at a crime scene in 1892 to secure what's considered the first criminal conviction based on fingerprint evidence.

examples.hanzi: 这个城市的罪案率下降了。
examples.pinyin: Zhège chéngshì de zuì'àn lǜ xiàjiàng le.
examples.english: The crime rate in this city has dropped.

examples.hanzi: 侦探小说里总有一桩神秘的罪案。
examples.pinyin: Zhēntàn xiǎoshuō lǐ zǒng yǒu yì zhuāng shénmì de zuì'àn.
examples.english: A detective novel always has a mysterious crime.

components.note: 力 (strength) — effort, as in 办, 助, 努: achievement takes effort.
工 (gōng) gives the exact sound; 工 also means work.

example.hanzi: 这次实验成功了。
example.pinyin: Zhè cì shíyàn chénggōng le.
example.english: This experiment succeeded.
example.fact: 功 gives 成功 (succeed), 功夫 (kung fu, and also time or effort), 功劳 (credit), 功能 (function) and 气功 (qigong).

examples.hanzi: 他的努力终于成功了。
examples.pinyin: Tā de nǔlì zhōngyú chénggōng le.
examples.english: His efforts finally succeeded.

examples.hanzi: 她每天练功，身体很好。
examples.pinyin: Tā měitiān liàngōng, shēntǐ hěn hǎo.
examples.english: She practices martial arts every day and has a healthy body.

components.note: 衣 (clothing) — clothes and wrapping: 装, 被, 衬; 袭 is to attack suddenly, an old sense of "cover over". 龙 is only a loose sound clue.

example.hanzi: 台风袭击了沿海地区。
example.pinyin: Táifēng xíjī le yánhǎi dìqū.
example.english: The typhoon struck the coastal areas.
example.fact: 袭 gives 袭击 (attack, also for storms), 偷袭 (sneak attack), 空袭 (air raid), 世袭 (hereditary) and 抄袭 (plagiarise).

examples.hanzi: 昨晚一场暴雨袭来了。
examples.pinyin: Zuówǎn yì chǎng bàoyǔ xílái le.
examples.english: A heavy rainstorm struck last night.

examples.hanzi: 他沿袭了家里的传统。
examples.pinyin: Tā yánxí le jiālǐ de chuántǒng.
examples.english: He carried on his family's tradition.

components.note: 大 (big) — marks size and swagger, as in 太 too, 夺; 夸 is to make something sound big, to boast.
亏 (kuī) hints at the sound: 夸 kuā is close to 垮 kuǎ and 跨 kuà.

example.hanzi: 老师夸我写得好。
example.pinyin: Lǎoshī kuā wǒ xiě de hǎo.
example.english: The teacher praised my writing.
example.fact: 夸 means both 'praise' (夸奖) and 'exaggerate' (夸张, 夸大). 夸 someone is the ordinary way to compliment them.

examples.hanzi: 大家都夸这道菜很好吃。
examples.pinyin: Dàjiā dōu kuā zhè dào cài hěn hǎochī.
examples.english: Everyone praised this dish for being delicious.

examples.hanzi: 他说话总爱夸大其词。
examples.pinyin: Tā shuōhuà zǒng ài kuādà qící.
examples.english: He always likes to exaggerate when he speaks.

components.note: 亡 (die, lose) — dictionary: a man in a coffin; early forms may be a person hiding or fleeing. Treat as a memory aid. It also gives sound clues in 忙 máng, 盲 máng.
亠 (lid) — the top. Memory aid: a lid closed over a person — gone, dead, as in 死亡.

example.hanzi: 这场事故造成两人死亡。
example.pinyin: Zhè chǎng shìgù zàochéng liǎng rén sǐwáng.
example.english: The accident caused two deaths.
example.fact: 亡 gives 死亡 (death), 逃亡 (flee), 灭亡 (perish) and 亡羊补牢 ('mend the pen after the sheep are lost', better late than never). Don't mix it up with 忙 (busy) and 忘 (forget).

examples.hanzi: 这场地震造成了很多人死亡。
examples.pinyin: Zhè chǎng dìzhèn zàochéng le hěn duō rén sǐwáng.
examples.english: This earthquake caused many deaths.

examples.hanzi: 他在那场战争中不幸身亡。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài nà chǎng zhànzhēng zhōng búxìng shēnwáng.
examples.english: He unfortunately died in that war.

components.note: 亻 (person) — person radical — 传 is something passed from person to person.
专 (zhuān) — near sound — 传 is chuán; 专 also sounds out 转 zhuǎn and 砖 zhuān.
单 (dān) gives sound to 弹 dàn/tán and 蝉 chán; as a word it means single, alone, a list.

example.hanzi: 志愿者在地铁站门口发传单。
example.pinyin: zhìyuànzhě zài dìtiězhàn ménkǒu fā chuándān.
example.english: Volunteers are handing out flyers at the subway station entrance.
example.fact: Johannes Gutenberg's mid-15th-century printing press didn't just enable books — it also made cheap, disposable single-sheet leaflets possible for the first time, and Martin Luther's 95 Theses spread rapidly across Europe partly because printers reproduced it as pamphlets and broadsides within weeks of 1517.

examples.hanzi: 商店门口有人在发传单。
examples.pinyin: Shāngdiàn ménkǒu yǒu rén zài fā chuándān.
examples.english: Someone is handing out flyers at the shop entrance.

examples.hanzi: 这张传单上有新店的地址。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhāng chuándān shàng yǒu xīn diàn de dìzhǐ.
examples.english: This flyer has the address of the new shop.

components.note: 冫 (ice) — marks cold and reduction, as in 冰, 冷, 冻; 减 is to lessen.
咸 (xián) hints at the sound: 减 jiǎn is close to 感 gǎn, 喊 hǎn and 碱 jiǎn.
辶 (movement, road) — 辶 marks going and moving — 速 is speed, as in 快速 and 速度.
束 (shù) — near sound — 速 is sù, same syllable with different initial.

example.hanzi: 前方施工，请提前减速。
example.pinyin: qiánfāng shīgōng, qǐng tíqián jiǎnsù.
example.english: Construction ahead — please slow down in advance.
example.fact: Regenerative braking, used in most modern electric and hybrid vehicles, converts the kinetic energy lost when a car slows down back into electricity stored in the battery, recovering energy that traditional friction brakes would otherwise waste entirely as heat.

examples.hanzi: 前面是学校，请减速慢行。
examples.pinyin: Qiánmiàn shì xuéxiào, qǐng jiǎnsù mànxíng.
examples.english: There's a school ahead; please slow down.

examples.hanzi: 司机看到红灯，立刻减速了。
examples.pinyin: Sījī kàndào hóngdēng, lìkè jiǎnsù le.
examples.english: The driver saw the red light and slowed down immediately.

components.note: 疒 (illness) — marks sickness, as in 病 ill, 疼 pain, 痛; 瘫 is paralysis, as in 瘫痪.
难 (nán) — only a loose sound hint (tān vs nán); same part in 摊 tān and 滩 tān.
疒 (illness) — marks sickness, as in 病, 疼; 痪 is numbness and paralysis, as in 瘫痪.
奂 (huàn) — same sound: 痪 huàn. 奂 also sounds out 换 huàn and 唤 huàn.

example.hanzi: 那场事故导致他下半身瘫痪。
example.pinyin: nà chǎng shìgù dǎozhì tā xiàbànshēn tānhuàn.
example.english: That accident left him paralyzed from the waist down.
example.fact: In 2014, scientists in Poland restored some mobility to a man paralyzed from a knife wound by transplanting olfactory ensheathing cells — cells that support nerve regeneration in the nose — directly into his damaged spinal cord, one of the first cases where a severed human spinal cord showed measurable functional repair.

examples.hanzi: 大雪使整个城市的交通瘫痪了。
examples.pinyin: Dàxuě shǐ zhěnggè chéngshì de jiāotōng tānhuàn le.
examples.english: The heavy snow paralyzed the traffic of the entire city.

examples.hanzi: 网络瘫痪了，大家都没法工作。
examples.pinyin: Wǎngluò tānhuàn le, dàjiā dōu méifǎ gōngzuò.
examples.english: The network went down and no one could work.

components.note: 黍 (millet) — the left part and radical, a grain plant. 黎 once meant 'black, many'; today it mostly appears in 巴黎 Paris and 黎明 dawn.
日 (sun) — the sun beside the moon: two light sources, so bright and clear.
月 (moon) — as in 朋, 期, 有; here it brightens the night.

example.hanzi: 渔民们在黎明前就出海捕鱼了。
example.pinyin: yúmínmen zài límíng qián jiù chūhǎi bǔyú le.
example.english: The fishermen went out to sea to fish before dawn.
example.fact: At the Arctic Circle in midsummer, the sun never fully sets, so there is effectively no dawn at all for weeks at a time — a phenomenon called the midnight sun — while in midwinter the same region can go without a proper sunrise for an equally long stretch, a stark contrast most of the world never experiences.

examples.hanzi: 黎明时分，天边出现了一道亮光。
examples.pinyin: Límíng shífēn, tiānbiān chūxiàn le yí dào liàngguāng.
examples.english: At dawn, a streak of light appeared on the horizon.

examples.hanzi: 我们在黎明前出发，爬上了山顶。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen zài límíng qián chūfā, pá shàng le shāndǐng.
examples.english: We set out before dawn and climbed to the top.

components.note: 阝 (mound, hill) — left-side 阝 is 阜 (mound), as in 阳, 院; 阿 first meant a slope.
可 (kě) — near sound — 阿 is ā; 可 also sounds out 河 hé and 哥 gē.
女 (woman) — 女 marks women and female roles, as in 妈 mom, 姐 sister, 姑 aunt; 姆 is a nanny, as in 保姆.
母 (mǔ) — same sound — 姆 is mǔ, just like 母 (mother).
斤 (axe) — the original idea was chopping with an axe, as in 新, 斩 chop, 断 break; today 斯 is mostly a sound-borrowing syllable sī in foreign names like 俄罗斯.
牛 (ox) — cattle and animals, as in 物 thing, 牧 herd, 牺 sacrifice: 特 first meant a bull, then special.
寺 (sì) is only a loose sound clue for tè; 寺 also in 诗 shī and 持 chí.
丹 (cinnabar) — an ancient picture of a mine with cinnabar in it; 丹 is red, as in 牡丹.

example.hanzi: 阿姆斯特丹有数百座桥梁横跨运河。
example.pinyin: Āmǔsītèdān yǒu shùbǎi zuò qiáoliáng héngkuà yùnhé.
example.english: Amsterdam has hundreds of bridges crossing its canals.
example.fact: Much of Amsterdam is built on land reclaimed from water and rests on wooden piles driven deep into the soft soil beneath the city — some of the oldest buildings still stand on foundation poles that are several centuries old, and their slow decay is a real concern for preserving the historic city center today.

examples.hanzi: 阿姆斯特丹是荷兰的首都。
examples.pinyin: Āmǔsītèdān shì Hélán de shǒudū.
examples.english: Amsterdam is the capital of the Netherlands.

examples.hanzi: 很多游客骑自行车游览阿姆斯特丹。
examples.pinyin: Hěn duō yóukè qí zìxíngchē yóulǎn Āmǔsītèdān.
examples.english: Many tourists tour Amsterdam by bicycle.

components.note: 页 (head, page) — marks the head, as in 顺, 领, 额; 顽 is a hard head, stubborn, as in 顽固.
元 (yuán) — loose sound hint (wán vs yuán); same part in 完 wán.
囗 (enclosure) — a walled-in border; 固 is something fenced in and firm, as in 国 country, 围 surround.
古 (gǔ) gives a close sound; it also sounds out 故 gù, 姑 gū and 苦 kǔ.

example.hanzi: 他对旧方法的坚持显得十分顽固。
example.pinyin: tā duì jiù fāngfǎ de jiānchí xiǎnde shífēn wángù.
example.english: His insistence on the old methods came across as very stubborn.
example.fact: Certain bacterial spores are so stubbornly resistant to destruction that some can survive boiling water and extreme drying — spores of Bacillus species have famously been revived in laboratory studies after being dormant for tens of thousands of years, and in some disputed claims, far longer.

examples.hanzi: 他太顽固了，谁劝都没用。
examples.pinyin: Tā tài wángù le, shéi quàn dōu méi yòng.
examples.english: He is so stubborn that no one's advice works.

examples.hanzi: 墙上的污渍很顽固，擦不掉。
examples.pinyin: Qiáng shàng de wūzì hěn wángù, cā bu diào.
examples.english: The stain on the wall is stubborn and can't be wiped off.

components.note: 圣 (holy) — traditional 聖 had an ear 耳 and a mouth 口: the sage who listens and speaks wisely.
母 (mother) — a woman 女 with two dots for breasts: a nursing mother. 母 also appears in 每 měi, 海 hǎi and 梅 méi.

example.hanzi: 这幅画描绘的是圣母抱着婴儿的场景。
example.pinyin: zhè fú huà miáohuì de shì shèngmǔ bào zhe yīng'ér de chǎngjǐng.
example.english: This painting depicts the scene of the Madonna holding an infant.
example.fact: Images of a mother goddess holding a child predate Christianity by thousands of years — the ancient Egyptian goddess Isis was frequently depicted nursing her son Horus, and many art historians argue this iconography directly influenced the visual conventions later used for paintings of the Madonna and Child.

examples.hanzi: 教堂里有一尊圣母像。
examples.pinyin: Jiàotáng lǐ yǒu yì zūn shèngmǔ xiàng.
examples.english: There is a statue of the Virgin Mary in the church.

examples.hanzi: 许多信徒向圣母祈祷。
examples.pinyin: Xǔduō xìntú xiàng shèngmǔ qídǎo.
examples.english: Many believers pray to the Holy Mother.

components.note: 心 (heart) — marks the mind and feelings, as in 想, 思, 意; 忽 is a lapse of attention, hence neglect or suddenly.
勿 (wù) is a loose hint for hū; 物 wù shares it.
灬 (fire) — heat and burning, as in 热 hot, 点 dot, 照 shine. 然 first meant "to burn" (燃 rán adds 火 later); "so, naturally" is borrowed.
肰 (rán) gives the exact sound and shows up in 燃 rán.

example.hanzi: 天空忽然变暗，下起了暴雨。
example.pinyin: tiānkōng hūrán biàn àn, xià qǐ le bàoyǔ.
example.english: The sky suddenly turned dark, and a heavy rain began to fall.
example.fact: Flash floods can turn a dry desert canyon into a raging torrent in a matter of minutes, even under a clear sky overhead, because the triggering storm may be falling many miles upstream — a hazard that makes canyons like those in Utah's Zion National Park especially dangerous to hikers caught off guard.

examples.hanzi: 他忽然想起自己忘了带钥匙。
examples.pinyin: Tā hūrán xiǎngqǐ zìjǐ wàng le dài yàoshi.
examples.english: He suddenly remembered that he had forgotten his keys.

examples.hanzi: 灯忽然灭了，屋里一片漆黑。
examples.pinyin: Dēng hūrán miè le, wū lǐ yí piàn qīhēi.
examples.english: The light suddenly went out, leaving the room pitch dark.

components.note: 鱼 (fish) — 鱼 is the fish radical, as in 鲨, 鲸; 鲜 pairs 鱼 with 羊 (sheep) — both freshly tasty foods, so fresh.
艹 (plants) — marks grasses and flowers, as in 草, 茶, 菜; 花 is a flower.
化 (huà) hints at the sound: 花 huā is close, and 化 also gives 华 huá and 货 huò.

example.hanzi: 他每周都会给妈妈送一束鲜花。
example.pinyin: tā měi zhōu dōu huì gěi māma sòng yì shù xiānhuā.
example.english: He gives his mother a bouquet of fresh flowers every week.
example.fact: The Netherlands exports more cut flowers than any other country in the world, and the Aalsmeer flower auction near Amsterdam is one of the largest flower markets on Earth, trading tens of millions of flowers and plants on a typical day before many are flown out to florists worldwide within 24 hours.

examples.hanzi: 花店里有各种各样的鲜花。
examples.pinyin: Huādiàn lǐ yǒu gèzhǒng-gèyàng de xiānhuā.
examples.english: The flower shop has all kinds of fresh flowers.

examples.hanzi: 他在她的生日那天送了一大束鲜花。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài tā de shēngrì nà tiān sòng le yí dà shù xiānhuā.
examples.english: On her birthday he sent a big bouquet of flowers.

components.note: ⺈ (bent figure) — top part, a person; with 口 and 儿 it forms 免. Origin unclear; Memory aid: a person with a hat slipping out, 'excused'.
儿 (legs) — the bottom part and radical, a walking person, as in 先 first and 兄 older brother.
彳 (step) — walking and going, as in 行, 往, 很 very.
寸 (hand) — oldest form is a hand grabbing a cowrie shell (money): 得 is "to obtain". The shell has worn down to 旦.

example.hanzi: 出门带把伞，免得下雨淋湿了。
example.pinyin: chūmén dài bǎ sǎn, miǎnde xiàyǔ lín shī le.
example.english: Bring an umbrella when you go out, so you won't get soaked if it rains.
example.fact: Lightning rods, invented by Benjamin Franklin in 1752, work by giving electrical current a low-resistance path to the ground, so a rod-equipped building is struck 'safely' instead of the current arcing destructively through the structure itself — a simple design that still protects most modern skyscrapers today.

examples.hanzi: 早点出门吧，免得迟到。
examples.pinyin: Zǎodiǎn chūmén ba, miǎnde chídào.
examples.english: Let's leave early so we won't be late.

examples.hanzi: 我给你留了便条，免得你找不到我。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ gěi nǐ liú le biàntiáo, miǎnde nǐ zhǎo bu dào wǒ.
examples.english: I left you a note so you wouldn't be unable to find me.

components.note: 上 (above) — a mark above a line, the mirror of 下 below.
千 (thousand) — 千 is a number built on the old form of 人 with an extra stroke; its sound is also in 迁 qiān.

example.hanzi: 这场演唱会吸引了上千名观众。
example.pinyin: zhè chǎng yǎnchànghuì xīyǐn le shàngqiān míng guānzhòng.
example.english: This concert attracted upwards of a thousand spectators.
example.fact: The Terracotta Army buried near China's first emperor, Qin Shi Huang, contains upwards of 8,000 life-sized clay soldiers, each with individually sculpted facial features — archaeologists believe many more may still lie unexcavated in the surrounding pits discovered since 1974.

examples.hanzi: 这个村子里有上千棵老树。
examples.pinyin: Zhège cūnzi lǐ yǒu shàngqiān kē lǎo shù.
examples.english: There are over a thousand old trees in this village.

examples.hanzi: 这座图书馆有上千本英文书。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zuò túshūguǎn yǒu shàngqiān běn Yīngwén shū.
examples.english: This library has over a thousand English books.

components.note: 土 (earth) — earth radical — a base is something solid on the ground, as in 地, 城, 块.
其 (qí) — loose hint — 基 is jī; 其 also sounds out 期 qī and 旗 qí.
目 (eye) — marks seeing and watching, as in 看, 眼, 睡; 督 is to oversee, to watch over.
叔 (shū) is a loose hint for dū.
彳 (step) — marks walking, as in 行, 往, 很, 得; 徒 pairs it with 走 walk: going on foot, then a follower.
走 (walk) — as in 跑 run, 起 rise.

example.hanzi: 他的祖父母是虔诚的基督徒。
example.pinyin: tā de zǔfùmǔ shì qiánchéng de Jīdūtú.
example.english: His grandparents are devout Christians.
example.fact: Christianity was still a minority, often persecuted faith within the Roman Empire for its first three centuries, until Emperor Constantine's Edict of Milan in 313 AD legalized it, and by the end of that same century it had become the empire's official state religion under Theodosius I.

examples.hanzi: 基督徒在圣诞节会去教堂。
examples.pinyin: Jīdūtú zài Shèngdànjié huì qù jiàotáng.
examples.english: Christians go to church at Christmas.

examples.hanzi: 这位基督徒每天晚上都读《圣经》。
examples.pinyin: Zhè wèi jīdūtú měi tiān wǎnshang dōu dú《Shèngjīng》.
examples.english: This Christian reads the Bible every night.

components.note: 力 (strength) — effort, as in 助, 男, 努: handling things takes effort. The two dots stand in for 辡 of the traditional 辦.
木 (tree) — wood, as in 桌, 树, 板: 案 is a wooden table.
安 (ān) is a close sound clue for àn; also in 按 àn.

example.hanzi: 这位律师办案经验丰富，从不轻易放弃。
example.pinyin: zhè wèi lǜshī bàn'àn jīngyàn fēngfù, cóng bù qīngyì fàngqì.
example.english: This lawyer has extensive experience handling cases and never gives up easily.
example.fact: DNA evidence, first used to help solve a criminal case in England in 1986, revolutionized how cases are handled — the same techniques have since been used by projects like the Innocence Project to exonerate hundreds of wrongfully convicted people, some of whom had already spent decades in prison.

examples.hanzi: 警察办案需要充足的证据。
examples.pinyin: Jǐngchá bàn'àn xūyào chōngzú de zhèngjù.
examples.english: Police need sufficient evidence to handle a case.

examples.hanzi: 他为了办案，几天几夜没有回家。
examples.pinyin: Tā wèile bàn'àn, jǐ tiān jǐ yè méiyǒu huíjiā.
examples.english: To work on the case, he didn't go home for days and nights.

components.note: 贝 (shell, old money) — marks money and trade, as in 财, 货, 贵; 贩 is to trade goods.
反 (fǎn) hints at the sound: 贩 fàn is close to 饭 fàn.
买 (mǎi, buy) — its sound is almost the same as 卖 mài, and the meaning is the opposite: buy and sell.

example.hanzi: 当地政府严厉打击非法贩卖野生动物的行为。
example.pinyin: dāngdì zhèngfǔ yánlì dǎjī fēifǎ fànmài yěshēng dòngwù de xíngwéi.
example.english: The local government is cracking down hard on the illegal trafficking of wild animals.
example.fact: The illegal wildlife trade is estimated by conservation groups to be worth billions of dollars a year, making it one of the largest illicit trades globally alongside drugs and arms — pangolins alone are believed to be the most trafficked mammal on Earth, prized largely for their scales in traditional medicine markets.

examples.hanzi: 他因为贩卖假货被抓了。
examples.pinyin: Tā yīnwèi fànmài jiǎhuò bèi zhuā le.
examples.english: He was caught for selling counterfeit goods.

examples.hanzi: 政府禁止贩卖未成年人不能买的东西。
examples.pinyin: Zhèngfǔ jìnzhǐ fànmài wèichéngniánrén bù néng mǎi de dōngxi.
examples.english: The government bans selling things that minors can't buy.

components.note: 入 (enter) — a pointed shape pushing in; not 人 (person), whose strokes spread outward.
犭 (animal, dog) — animals, as in 狗 dog, 猫 cat, 狂 wild: dogs guard.
讠 (speech) — words and law; 狱 first meant a lawsuit, then a prison.

example.hanzi: 他因为诈骗罪被判入狱五年。
example.pinyin: tā yīnwèi zhàpiànzuì bèi pàn rùyù wǔ nián.
example.english: He was sentenced to five years in prison for fraud.
example.fact: The United States has the highest documented incarceration rate of any country in the world, holding roughly 20% of the world's prisoners despite having only about 4% of the global population, according to figures widely cited by criminal justice researchers.

examples.hanzi: 他入狱以后，家人每个月去看他。
examples.pinyin: Tā rùyù yǐhòu, jiārén měi gè yuè qù kàn tā.
examples.english: After he went to prison, his family visited him every month.

examples.hanzi: 这个案子的主犯已经入狱了。
examples.pinyin: Zhège ànzi de zhǔfàn yǐjīng rùyù le.
examples.english: The main culprit in this case has already gone to prison.

components.note: 止 (foot) — a person 人 standing on tiptoe 止 to see farther; hence to aspire or plan (企图), also 企业 enterprise.
鸟 (bird) — marks birds, as in 鸡 chicken, 鸭 duck; 鹅 is the goose, as in 企鹅 penguin.
我 (wǒ) — only a loose sound hint (é vs wǒ); same part in 俄 é and 饿 è.

example.hanzi: 南极的企鹅群在冰面上排成长队行走。
example.pinyin: Nánjí de qǐ'é qún zài bīngmiàn shàng pái chéng chángduì xíngzǒu.
example.english: The colony of penguins in Antarctica walks in a long line across the ice.
example.fact: Emperor penguins can dive deeper than 500 meters and hold their breath for over 20 minutes while hunting, thanks to a slowed heart rate and specialized hemoglobin that lets their bodies keep functioning on far less oxygen than most air-breathing animals could tolerate.

examples.hanzi: 动物园里的企鹅很可爱。
examples.pinyin: Dòngwùyuán lǐ de qǐ'é hěn kě'ài.
examples.english: The penguins at the zoo are very cute.

examples.hanzi: 企鹅走路的样子摇摇摆摆的。
examples.pinyin: Qǐ'é zǒulù de yàngzi yáoyáo-bǎibǎi de.
examples.english: Penguins waddle when they walk.

components.note: 比 (compare) — two people side by side, one lined up with the other; to compare.
口 (mouth) — marks speech, sounds and eating, as in 叫 call, 吃 eat, 唱 sing; 喻 is saying one thing in terms of another, as in 比喻 metaphor.
俞 (yú) — close sound: 喻 yù. 俞 also sounds out 愉 yú and 偷 tōu.

example.hanzi: 老师用了一个生动的比喻来解释这个概念。
example.pinyin: lǎoshī yòng le yí gè shēngdòng de bǐyù lái jiěshì zhège gàiniàn.
example.english: The teacher used a vivid metaphor to explain this concept.
example.fact: Cognitive linguists George Lakoff and Mark Johnson argued in their influential 1980 book 'Metaphors We Live By' that metaphor isn't just a literary decoration but a fundamental way human thought is structured — for example, the pervasive metaphor of 'time is money' shapes how English speakers talk about spending, wasting, and saving time, not just cash.

examples.hanzi: 这只是一个比喻，别当真。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhǐshì yí gè bǐyù, bié dàngzhēn.
examples.english: This is just a metaphor; don't take it literally.

examples.hanzi: “时间就是金钱”是一个常见的比喻。
examples.pinyin: "Shíjiān jiù shì jīnqián" shì yí gè chángjiàn de bǐyù.
examples.english: "Time is money" is a common metaphor.

components.note: 女 (woman) — with a hand 又, a seized person: a slave. 奴 nú also sounds out 努 nǔ and 怒 nù.

example.hanzi: 他不想做金钱的奴隶。
example.pinyin: Tā bù xiǎng zuò jīnqián de núlì.
example.english: He doesn't want to be a slave to money.
example.fact: 奴 gives 奴隶 (slave), 奴才 (lackey), 农奴 (serf). Modern slang uses it for people tied down: 房奴 (mortgage slave).

examples.hanzi: 他不愿意做金钱的奴隶。
examples.pinyin: Tā bú yuànyì zuò jīnqián de núlì.
examples.english: He does not want to be a slave to money.

examples.hanzi: 她成了手机的奴隶。
examples.pinyin: Tā chéng le shǒujī de núlì.
examples.english: She has become a slave to her phone.

components.note: 氵 (water, 三点水) — marks water and liquids, as in 海 sea, 河 river, 汤 soup; 泼 is splashing or pouring water.
发 (fā) — close sound: 泼 pō. 发 also sounds out 拨 bō and 废 fèi.

example.hanzi: 别往地上泼水。
example.pinyin: Bié wǎng dì shang pō shuǐ.
example.english: Don't splash water on the ground.
example.fact: 泼 gives 泼水节 (the Water-Splashing Festival), 泼冷水 ('to pour cold water', as in English) and 活泼 (lively).

examples.hanzi: 他不小心把水泼在了我身上。
examples.pinyin: Tā bù xiǎoxīn bǎ shuǐ pō zài le wǒ shēnshang.
examples.english: He accidentally splashed water on me.

examples.hanzi: 新年时有人泼水祝福。
examples.pinyin: Xīnnián shí yǒu rén pōshuǐ zhùfú.
examples.english: At New Year some people splash water as a blessing.

components.note: 氵 (water, 三点水) — marks water, as in 海 sea, 河 river; 湖 is a lake.
胡 (hú) — same sound: 湖 hú. 胡 also sounds out 糊 hú and 蝴 hú.
辶 (walk) — movement and roads, as in 过, 近, 送: following the edge. The part 力 stands in for 臱 in the traditional 邊.

example.hanzi: 他们在湖边搭了一个帐篷过夜。
example.pinyin: tāmen zài húbiān dā le yí gè zhàngpéng guòyè.
example.english: They set up a tent by the lakeside to spend the night.
example.fact: Lake Baikal in Siberia, the deepest lake in the world at over 1,600 meters, holds roughly 20% of all the unfrozen fresh water on Earth's surface — more than all five of North America's Great Lakes combined.

examples.hanzi: 我们在湖边散步，看到了很多天鹅。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen zài húbiān sànbù, kàndào le hěn duō tiān'é.
examples.english: We took a walk by the lake and saw many swans.

examples.hanzi: 湖边的咖啡馆很安静。
examples.pinyin: Húbiān de kāfēiguǎn hěn ānjìng.
examples.english: The café by the lake is very quiet.

components.note: 身 (body) — a person's body with a rounded belly. As a radical it marks body words: 躺 lie down, 躲 hide, 躯 body.
方 (fāng) is a near sound match for páng (-ang); 方 also sounds out 房 fáng and 防 fáng.

example.hanzi: 无论遇到什么困难，她都会陪在他身旁。
example.pinyin: wúlùn yù dào shénme kùnnán, tā dōu huì péi zài tā shēnpáng.
example.english: No matter what difficulties arise, she will stay by his side.
example.fact: Emperor penguins and many other cold-climate animals use a behavior called huddling, pressing close against the animals beside them, to conserve body heat so effectively that the center of a huddle can be around 20 degrees Celsius warmer than the surrounding air during Antarctic winters.

examples.hanzi: 他坐在我身旁，一句话也没说。
examples.pinyin: Tā zuò zài wǒ shēnpáng, yí jù huà yě méi shuō.
examples.english: He sat next to me without saying a word.

examples.hanzi: 孩子们都围在老师的身旁。
examples.pinyin: Háizimen dōu wéi zài lǎoshī de shēnpáng.
examples.english: The children all gathered around the teacher.

components.note: 中 (middle) — a line through the middle of a box, a centre mark. 中 gives sound to 钟 zhōng, 种 zhǒng, 忠 zhōng and 衷 zhōng.
辶 (movement) — marks roads and travel, as in 过, 进, 送; 途 is a road or route.
余 (yú) is a loose hint for tú; 涂 tú shares it.

example.hanzi: 飞机因为天气原因中途改变了航线。
example.pinyin: fēijī yīnwèi tiānqì yuányīn zhōngtú gǎibiàn le hángxiàn.
example.english: The plane changed its route midway due to weather conditions.
example.fact: The Apollo 13 mission became one of the most famous mid-flight crises in space history when an oxygen tank exploded roughly 56 hours into the flight, forcing the crew to abandon their moon landing and improvise a survival plan using the lunar module as a lifeboat for the trip back to Earth.

examples.hanzi: 火车在中途停了十分钟。
examples.pinyin: Huǒchē zài zhōngtú tíng le shí fēnzhōng.
examples.english: The train stopped for ten minutes midway.

examples.hanzi: 他在中途改变了主意。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài zhōngtú gǎibiàn le zhǔyi.
examples.english: He changed his mind halfway through.

components.note: 力 (strength) — with 口 mouth: adding strength by words, hence to add, to increase. 加 also in 架 jià and 驾 jià.
王 (jade, 玉 with its dot dropped) — a blade 刂 cutting two jades apart: to divide into groups, hence class or shift.

example.hanzi: 为了赶项目进度，团队这周每天都要加班。
example.pinyin: wèile gǎn xiàngmù jìndù, tuánduì zhè zhōu měitiān dōu yào jiābān.
example.english: To meet the project deadline, the team has to work overtime every day this week.
example.fact: Japan has a specific legal and medical term, karoshi, meaning 'death from overwork,' recognized since the late 1980s to describe fatal strokes, heart attacks, or suicides linked directly to extreme work hours — the government now publishes an annual white paper tracking related labor cases.

examples.hanzi: 我今晚要加班，不能和你们吃饭了。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ jīnwǎn yào jiābān, bù néng hé nǐmen chīfàn le.
examples.english: I have to work overtime tonight and can't have dinner with you.

examples.hanzi: 他常常加班到很晚才回家。
examples.pinyin: Tā chángcháng jiābān dào hěn wǎn cái huíjiā.
examples.english: He often works overtime until very late before getting home.

components.note: 勹 (wrap) — a person curled around something; in 包 it wraps around a baby 巳, the original picture. 包 sounds out 抱 bào, 跑 pǎo, 泡 pào, 饱 bǎo.
口 (mouth) — holding something in the mouth; also in 吃 eat, 吞 swallow.
今 (jīn) is a loose clue; it also sounds out 贪 tān and 琴 qín.

example.hanzi: 这份套餐包含早餐和晚餐。
example.pinyin: zhè fèn tàocān bāohán zǎocān hé wǎncān.
example.english: This package includes breakfast and dinner.
example.fact: The observable universe is estimated to include roughly two trillion galaxies, according to a 2016 analysis of deep Hubble Space Telescope images — a figure roughly ten times higher than earlier estimates, showing how much even 'complete' astronomical surveys can still be missing.

examples.hanzi: 这本书包含了很多有用的知识。
examples.pinyin: Zhè běn shū bāohán le hěn duō yǒuyòng de zhīshi.
examples.english: This book contains lots of useful knowledge.

examples.hanzi: 房租里包含水电费吗？
examples.pinyin: Fángzū lǐ bāohán shuǐdiànfèi ma?
examples.english: Does the rent include utilities?

components.note: 亚 (yà) — Asia; as a part it sounds out 哑 yǎ and 娅 yà.
力 (lì) sounds exactly like 历 — simplified 历 replaced complex 歷 with 力 for the sound; meaning is passing through time.
山 (mountain) — a picture of three peaks; as a radical it marks hills, as in 岛, 峰, 岸.
大 (big) — a front-facing person with arms and legs spread wide: big. As radical, 大 is in 天 sky, 太 too much, 夫 man.

example.hanzi: 亚历山大大帝在三十岁前就征服了大半个已知世界。
example.pinyin: Yàlìshāndà dàdì zài sānshí suì qián jiù zhēngfú le dàbàn gè yǐzhī shìjiè.
example.english: Alexander the Great had conquered most of the known world before he turned thirty.
example.fact: Alexander the Great founded more than 20 cities across his empire, many named Alexandria after himself — the most famous, in Egypt, later became home to one of the ancient world's greatest libraries and a major center of scholarship for centuries after his death in 323 BC.

examples.hanzi: 亚历山大是我们班的班长。
examples.pinyin: Yàlìshāndà shì wǒmen bān de bānzhǎng.
examples.english: Alexander is our class monitor.

examples.hanzi: 我朋友亚历山大住在莫斯科。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ péngyou Yàlìshāndà zhù zài Mòsīkē.
examples.english: My friend Alexander lives in Moscow.

components.note: 农 (farming) — simplified from 農, which showed a tool 辰 working a field 田; 农 is farming, as in 农民.
民 (people) — one old theory sees an eye pierced by a pointed tool, a mark of those with no rights; the meaning "ordinary people" is what to remember.

example.hanzi: 这位农民种了三十年的水稻。
example.pinyin: zhè wèi nóngmín zhòngle sānshí nián de shuǐdào.
example.english: This farmer has grown rice for thirty years.
example.fact: Rice paddies flooded with water create an unusual ecosystem where farmers in parts of Asia raise fish or ducks alongside the crop — the animals eat pests and weeds while their waste fertilizes the soil, a practice called rice-fish co-culture that dates back over 1,700 years in China's Qingtian region, recognized today as a UNESCO-listed Globally Important Agricultural Heritage System.

examples.hanzi: 农民们在地里忙着收麦子。
examples.pinyin: Nóngmínmen zài dì lǐ mángzhe shōu màizi.
examples.english: The farmers are busy harvesting wheat in the fields.

examples.hanzi: 政府给农民发放了新的补贴。
examples.pinyin: Zhèngfǔ gěi nóngmín fāfàng le xīn de bǔtiē.
examples.english: The government gave farmers new subsidies.

components.note: 萬 (traditional ten thousand) — 万 is the simplified form of 萬, which pictured a scorpion borrowed for the number 10,000; 万 also sounds out 迈 mài.
能 (can) — originally a picture of a bear, a strong animal (熊 xióng adds fire 灬); "strong, able" gave "can".

example.hanzi: 这把万能钥匙能打开大楼里所有的门。
example.pinyin: zhè bǎ wànnéng yàoshi néng dǎkāi dàlóu lǐ suǒyǒu de mén.
example.english: This master key can open every door in the building.
example.fact: Locksmiths' "bump keys" exploit a real mechanical weakness in most pin-tumbler locks: a sharp rap on a specially cut key jolts the pins upward just long enough for the cylinder to turn, letting a single blank open thousands of different locks — a vulnerability documented since the 1970s and still a factor in modern lock design.

examples.hanzi: 这个万能充电器可以给各种手机充电。
examples.pinyin: Zhège wànnéng chōngdiànqì kěyǐ gěi gè zhǒng shǒujī chōngdiàn.
examples.english: This universal charger can charge all kinds of phones.

examples.hanzi: 没有人是万能的，大家都需要帮助。
examples.pinyin: Méiyǒu rén shì wànnéng de, dàjiā dōu xūyào bāngzhù.
examples.english: No one is all-powerful; everybody needs help.

components.note: 萬 (traditional ten thousand) — 万 is the simplified form of 萬, which pictured a scorpion borrowed for the number 10,000; 万 also sounds out 迈 mài.
刀 (knife) — cutting, as in 切, 刻, 到: a blade splits.
八 (eight) — originally two lines pulling apart: divide. 分 also gives 份 fèn, 粉 fěn and 纷 fēn.

example.hanzi: 听到这个消息，她万分激动。
example.pinyin: tīngdào zhège xiāoxi, tā wànfēn jīdòng.
example.english: Hearing this news, she was extremely excited.
example.fact: The adrenaline surge behind intense excitement is produced by the adrenal medulla in under two seconds, triggering a heart-rate spike that can exceed 180 beats per minute — a response shaped by the same fight-or-flight pathway that let early humans react instantly to predators.

examples.hanzi: 我万分感谢你的帮助。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ wànfēn gǎnxiè nǐ de bāngzhù.
examples.english: I am extremely grateful for your help.

examples.hanzi: 她对这次误会感到万分抱歉。
examples.pinyin: Tā duì zhè cì wùhuì gǎndào wànfēn bàoqiàn.
examples.english: She felt extremely sorry about this misunderstanding.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — a picture of an open mouth; as a radical it appears in characters of speech, eating and sounds — 吃, 喝, 叫, 吗.
纟 (silk, thread) — simplified 糸 (silk); colours came from dyed silk, as in 绿, 紫, 给.
工 (gōng) — near sound — 红 is hóng; 工 also sounds out 江 jiāng and 空 kōng.

example.hanzi: 她出门前总要涂一点口红。
example.pinyin: tā chūmén qián zǒng yào tú yìdiǎn kǒuhóng.
example.english: She always puts on a little lipstick before going out.
example.fact: Lipstick is one of the oldest cosmetics on record: Sumerian women in ancient Mesopotamia crushed semi-precious gems into powder to redden their lips around 3500 BC, and Cleopatra later favored a red dye made from crushed carmine beetles and ants — a pigment chemically related to the carmine still used in some lipsticks today.

examples.hanzi: 这支口红的颜色很漂亮。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhī kǒuhóng de yánsè hěn piàoliang.
examples.english: The color of this lipstick is very pretty.

examples.hanzi: 妈妈送了我一支口红做生日礼物。
examples.pinyin: Māma sòng le wǒ yì zhī kǒuhóng zuò shēngrì lǐwù.
examples.english: Mom gave me a lipstick as a birthday present.

components.note: 十 (ten, many) — traditional 協 pairs 十 with three 力 (strength) side by side: many forces joined in effort, so cooperation.
讠 (speech) — words and language, as in 说, 请, 谢.
周 (zhōu) is a loose sound clue for diào/tiáo; 周 also in 凋 diāo.

example.hanzi: 教练负责协调球队的训练计划。
example.pinyin: jiàoliàn fùzé xiétiáo qiúduì de xùnliàn jìhuà.
example.english: The coach is responsible for coordinating the team's training schedule.
example.fact: The human cerebellum, which makes up only about 10% of brain volume, contains roughly 80% of the brain's neurons and is the primary structure responsible for coordinating fine muscle movement — damage to it produces a distinctive unsteady gait known as cerebellar ataxia.

examples.hanzi: 这件事需要各部门之间好好协调。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn shì xūyào gè bùmén zhījiān hǎohāo xiétiáo.
examples.english: This matter requires good coordination between departments.

examples.hanzi: 他的动作很协调，跳舞跳得非常好。
examples.pinyin: Tā de dòngzuò hěn xiétiáo, tiàowǔ tiào de fēicháng hǎo.
examples.english: His movements are well coordinated, and he dances very well.

components.note: 王 (king) — the ruler below the crown-like top: 皇 is an emperor, as in 皇帝.
皇 (huáng) as a part sounds out 凰 huáng, 煌 huáng and 惶 huáng.
帝 (dì) is a sound clue for 蒂 dì (stem base) and 啼 tí; the old shape is possibly a flower calyx, uncertain.

example.hanzi: 秦始皇是中国历史上第一位皇帝。
example.pinyin: Qín Shǐhuáng shì Zhōngguó lìshǐ shàng dì yī wèi huángdì.
example.english: Qin Shi Huang was the first emperor in Chinese history.
example.fact: When Qin Shi Huang died in 210 BC, he was buried with an army of over 8,000 life-size terracotta soldiers, each with individually sculpted facial features, discovered by farmers digging a well in 1974 near Xi'an — one of the largest archaeological finds of the 20th century.

examples.hanzi: 这位皇帝在位时间很长。
examples.pinyin: Zhè wèi huángdì zàiwèi shíjiān hěn cháng.
examples.english: This emperor reigned for a long time.

examples.hanzi: 故宫是古代皇帝住的地方。
examples.pinyin: Gùgōng shì gǔdài huángdì zhù de dìfang.
examples.english: The Forbidden City is where ancient emperors lived.

components.note: 正 (zhèng) is a close sound clue for zhěng; 正 also means correct, fitting for putting things in order.
攵 (tap, strike) — hand with stick, as in 教, 收, 改: setting things right by force.
夕 (evening) — 夕 is evening or dusk, as in 外, 多, 梦; 夜 is night.
亦 (yì) — near sound — 夜 is yè; 夜 also sounds out 液 yè.

example.hanzi: 他整夜都没有睡着。
example.pinyin: tā zhěngyè dōu méiyǒu shuìzháo.
example.english: He didn't fall asleep the whole night.
example.fact: A single night of total sleep deprivation measurably impairs reaction time and judgment to a degree comparable with a blood alcohol content around 0.05%, according to sleep researchers — one reason many countries now treat drowsy driving as seriously as drunk driving in road-safety campaigns.

examples.hanzi: 为了赶报告，他整夜没有休息。
examples.pinyin: Wèile gǎn bàogào, tā zhěngyè méiyǒu xiūxi.
examples.english: To finish the report, he didn't rest all night.

examples.hanzi: 外面整夜都在下雨。
examples.pinyin: Wàimiàn zhěngyè dōu zài xià yǔ.
examples.english: It rained all night outside.

components.note: 比 (compare) — two people side by side, one lined up with the other; to compare.
艹 (grass, plants) — the plant radical, as in 花 flower, 草 grass. In 萨 it no longer carries meaning; 萨 only appears in transliterations such as 菩萨 bodhisattva.
产 (to produce) — the lower right part. Memory aid: sound-only character; learn it as a unit from 菩萨, 萨克斯.

example.hanzi: 我们周末想订一份比萨。
example.pinyin: wǒmen zhōumò xiǎng dìng yí fèn bǐsà.
example.english: We want to order a pizza this weekend.
example.fact: The Margherita pizza, topped with tomato, mozzarella, and basil to mirror the colors of the Italian flag, was reportedly created in Naples in 1889 in honor of Queen Margherita of Savoy — a founding story still printed on pizzerias' walls throughout the city today.

examples.hanzi: 我们叫了一个大比萨，大家一起分着吃。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen jiào le yí gè dà bǐsà, dàjiā yìqǐ fēnzhe chī.
examples.english: We ordered a big pizza and shared it.

examples.hanzi: 这家店的比萨饼皮很薄。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā diàn de bǐsà bǐngpí hěn báo.
examples.english: The crust of this shop's pizza is very thin.

components.note: 今 (now, today) — gives sound to 琴 qín, 含 hán, 念 niàn and 吟 yín; the old picture is uncertain.
夕 (evening) — 夕 is evening or dusk, as in 外, 多, 梦; 夜 is night.
亦 (yì) — near sound — 夜 is yè; 夜 also sounds out 液 yè.

example.hanzi: 今夜的月亮特别圆。
example.pinyin: jīnyè de yuèliàng tèbié yuán.
example.english: Tonight's moon is especially round.
example.fact: A full moon looks measurably larger and brighter near the horizon than high overhead — an illusion called the "moon illusion" that has puzzled scientists for centuries, since photographs prove the moon's actual angular size stays constant no matter where it sits in the sky.

examples.hanzi: 今夜有雨，别忘了关窗。
examples.pinyin: Jīnyè yǒu yǔ, bié wàng le guān chuāng.
examples.english: It will rain tonight, so don't forget to close the window.

examples.hanzi: 今夜我们一起看星星吧。
examples.pinyin: Jīnyè wǒmen yìqǐ kàn xīngxing ba.
examples.english: Let's watch the stars together tonight.

components.note: 攵 (tap, strike) — hand with stick, as in 教, 改, 放: to gather by force or hand.
丩 (jiū) is only a loose sound clue for shōu.
买 (simplified 買) — the old form shows a net 网 over a shell 贝 (money): netting goods, to buy. 卖 mài sell is built on 买.

example.hanzi: 有人试图收买这位法官。
example.pinyin: yǒurén shìtú shōumǎi zhè wèi fǎguān.
example.english: Someone tried to bribe this judge.
example.fact: Transparency International's Corruption Perceptions Index, first published in 1995, ranks over 180 countries each year by perceived public-sector corruption; consistently top-ranked nations like Denmark and New Zealand share features such as strong freedom-of-information laws and independent judiciaries that make bribery harder to conceal.

examples.hanzi: 他想用钱收买这位证人。
examples.pinyin: Tā xiǎng yòng qián shōumǎi zhè wèi zhèngrén.
examples.english: He wants to buy off this witness with money.

examples.hanzi: 他们用小礼物收买了人心。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen yòng xiǎo lǐwù shōumǎi le rénxīn.
examples.english: They won people over with small gifts.

components.note: 廾 (two hands) — hands lifting an offering: to present respectfully. 奉 also sounds out 捧 pěng and 俸 fèng.

example.hanzi: 他奉命去北京开会。
example.pinyin: Tā fèngmìng qù Běijīng kāihuì.
example.english: He went to Beijing for a meeting by order.
example.fact: 奉 is formal: 奉献 (dedicate), 奉命 (by order), 奉承 (flatter) and 信奉 (to believe in). 无可奉告 is the official 'no comment'.

examples.hanzi: 领导奉命去外地出差。
examples.pinyin: Lǐngdǎo fèngmìng qù wàidì chūchāi.
examples.english: The leader went on a business trip on orders.

examples.hanzi: 请接受我奉上的礼物。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng jiēshòu wǒ fèngshàng de lǐwù.
examples.english: Please accept the gift I respectfully present.

components.note: 穴 (cave, hole) — creeping in through a hole; also in 空 empty, 窗 window.
切 (qiè) gives the exact sound.

example.hanzi: 小偷窃走了他的钱包。
example.pinyin: Xiǎotōu qièzǒu le tā de qiánbāo.
example.english: The thief stole his wallet.
example.fact: 窃 gives 盗窃 (theft), 窃听 (eavesdrop), 窃取 (steal), 窃笑 (snicker) and 窃喜 (secretly pleased).

examples.hanzi: 小偷窃取了他的银行卡密码。
examples.pinyin: Xiǎotōu qièqǔ le tā de yínhángkǎ mìmǎ.
examples.english: The thief stole his bank card password.

examples.hanzi: 她站在门外窃听他们的谈话。
examples.pinyin: Tā zhàn zài mén wài qiètīng tāmen de tánhuà.
examples.english: She stood outside and eavesdropped on their conversation.

components.note: 夕 (evening) — the left part, the time-of-day family as in 夜, 多, 梦. Memory aid: things done at night are outside the ordinary.
卜 (divination) — Dictionary story: night 夕 divination 卜, strange and 'outside'. A hedged mnemonic: 外面 outside, 另外 in addition.
凵 (open pit) — oldest form shows a foot stepping out of a pit or cave: to go out, come out.

example.hanzi: 下雨了，他们决定不外出了。
example.pinyin: xiàyǔ le, tāmen juédìng bù wàichū le.
example.english: It's raining, so they decided not to go out.
example.fact: Storm clouds that produce heavy rain, called cumulonimbus clouds, can tower more than 12 kilometers into the atmosphere and contain enough water to fill hundreds of thousands of swimming pools — their rapid updrafts of over 160 km/h also generate the electrical charge separation behind lightning.

examples.hanzi: 他今天外出办事，下午才回来。
examples.pinyin: Tā jīntiān wàichū bànshì, xiàwǔ cái huílái.
examples.english: He is out on business today and will be back in the afternoon.

examples.hanzi: 外出旅行时，请带好证件。
examples.pinyin: Wàichū lǚxíng shí, qǐng dài hǎo zhèngjiàn.
examples.english: When traveling, please bring your ID.

components.note: 凯 (kǎi) — triumph, mostly seen in names; as a part it sounds out 铠 kǎi and 恺 kǎi.
扌 (hand radical, 提手旁) — actions by hand: 打, 拉, 推; 撒 is scattering or letting go.
散 (sàn) scatter is the meaning-sound part: a hand 扌 scattering, with sā/sàn close in sound.

example.hanzi: 凯撒是古罗马著名的将军和政治家。
example.pinyin: Kǎisā shì gǔ Luómǎ zhùmíng de jiāngjūn hé zhèngzhìjiā.
example.english: Caesar was a famous general and statesman of ancient Rome.
example.fact: Julius Caesar's assassination on the Ides of March, 44 BC, was carried out by roughly 60 senators who reportedly stabbed him 23 times, yet a later Roman physician determined that only one wound — a chest stab — was actually fatal, with the rest inflicted after he had already collapsed.

examples.hanzi: 凯撒是罗马历史上很重要的人物。
examples.pinyin: Kǎisā shì Luómǎ lìshǐ shàng hěn zhòngyào de rénwù.
examples.english: Caesar is a very important figure in Roman history.

examples.hanzi: 他点了一份凯撒沙拉。
examples.pinyin: Tā diǎn le yí fèn Kǎisā shālā.
examples.english: He ordered a Caesar salad.

components.note: 亻 (person radical, 单人旁) — people and roles: 你, 他, 位; 代 is one person replacing another, then a generation.
弋 (yì) is only a loose hint; 代 itself sounds out 袋 dài and 贷 dài.
口 (mouth) — speaking, shouting: 叫, 吗, 喊; 号 is to call out, then a call-sign or number.
丂 (kǎo) is only a loose clue; it also appears in 考 kǎo and 巧 qiǎo.

example.hanzi: 这次行动的代号是"曙光"。
example.pinyin: zhè cì xíngdòng de dàihào shì "shǔguāng".
example.english: This operation's code name is "Dawn."
example.fact: The 1944 Normandy invasion carried the code name "Operation Overlord," and to protect it Allied intelligence ran an elaborate deception campaign called Operation Fortitude — complete with inflatable tanks and fake radio traffic — that convinced German commanders the real attack would come at Calais, not Normandy.

examples.hanzi: 这个项目的代号是“蓝鸟”。
examples.pinyin: Zhège xiàngmù de dàihào shì "lánniǎo".
examples.english: This project's code name is "Bluebird".

examples.hanzi: 在游戏里，我的代号是“小白”。
examples.pinyin: Zài yóuxì lǐ, wǒ de dàihào shì "xiǎo bái".
examples.english: In the game, my code name is "Xiaobai".

components.note: 钅 (metal) — 钅 is the simplified 金 (metal), as in 钱, 铁; 镇 first meant to weigh down with metal.
真 (zhēn) — near sound — 镇 is zhèn; 真 also sounds out 慎 shèn and 填 tián.
青 (qīng) hints at the -ing rhyme; same part in 清 请 情 晴 精. The 争 (contend) half is not a reliable clue.
刂 (knife) — marks cutting and dividing, as in 别, 刻; 剂 is a measured dose, as in 药剂 medicine.
齐 (qí) — loose sound hint (jì vs qí); 齐 also means even, fitting a measured dose.

example.hanzi: 医生给病人开了一些镇静剂。
example.pinyin: yīshēng gěi bìngrén kāile yìxiē zhènjìngjì.
example.english: The doctor prescribed some tranquilizers for the patient.
example.fact: Diazepam, sold under the brand name Valium, became the best-selling prescription drug in the United States for much of the 1970s, at one point accounting for over 2 billion pills sold annually — a scale of use that later prompted tighter regulation of benzodiazepine tranquilizers worldwide.

examples.hanzi: 他吃了镇静剂，很快就睡着了。
examples.pinyin: Tā chī le zhènjìngjì, hěn kuài jiù shuìzháo le.
examples.english: He took a sedative and fell asleep soon.

examples.hanzi: 医生说不能随便服用镇静剂。
examples.pinyin: Yīshēng shuō bù néng suíbiàn fúyòng zhènjìngjì.
examples.english: The doctor said sedatives must not be taken casually.
